newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - February 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - February 13.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Thursday's Daily Variety:

* Universal International Television has signed a nearly $100 million deal with France's top-rated station TF1 for future hour series, TV movies and feature films, which is being called the largest volume arrangement ever between an American studio and a private French broadcaster.

* The Clinton Administration revealed Wednesday for the first time that it would allow broadcasters to hold onto their current channels until 2006, one year longer than it had previously said. Commerce Department official Larry Irving said the additional year was added to ensure that broadcasters would have 10 years to make the transition from analog to digital TV before their current spectrum is repossessed by the government and sold at auction.

* New Line Television has begun drawing up the programming and marketing blueprints to transform "Lost in Space," the $70 million theatrical version of the 1965-68 cult CBS TV series, into a Star Trek-type franchise. New Line TV president Bob Friedman said he is negotiating with a broadcast network to produce an animated TV series and a live-action series.
* Earvin "Magic" Johnson, who owns a chain of movie theaters, is finalizing a deal to produce films at News Corp's Fox.

* Claire Danes, last seen being wooed by Leonardo DiCaprio in William Shakespeare's "Romeo & Juliet," will move into the film version of Victor Hugo's "Les Miserables" for Sony-based Mandalay Entertainment, sources said Wednesday. The picture starts shooting under Bille August's direction April 1 in Paris and then moves to Prague.
* "Murphy Brown" on Westinghouse's CBS will return for a 10th season, giving the Eye web one less worry as it starts thinking about the 1997-98 TV season.

* If Roderick Jaynes wins an Oscar March 24 as editor of "Fargo," don't be surprised if the trophy is accepted by the film's director and producer Joel and Ethan Coen. That's because Jaynes might be the only nominee this year who doesn't exist: sources said it's a pseudonym for the filmmaking brothers.
